question: ‘Once a Dancer’ is the autobiography of ________________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Allegra Kent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Allegra Kent** is a renowned American ballet dancer and writer, best known for her work with the New York City Ballet.
 
• Her autobiography, *Once a Dancer*, was published in **1997**, detailing her extraordinary life and career in ballet.
 
• Allegra Kent was a muse to **George Balanchine**, one of the greatest choreographers of the 20th century.
 
• She performed in iconic ballets such as *The Nutcracker*, *Agon*, and *Jewels*, leaving a lasting legacy in the world of dance.
 
• Her book provides insights into the physical and emotional demands of being a professional dancer, along with her personal struggles and triumphs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **George Balanchine**

 
 
• Often called the father of American ballet, Balanchine was a Russian-born choreographer who co-founded the New York City Ballet.
 
• His innovative choreography reshaped ballet, blending classical techniques with modern styles.
 
• He created numerous masterpieces, including *Serenade*, *Concerto Barocco*, and *Apollo*.
 
 
 
• **Ballet Terminology**
 
 
• **Pas de Deux:** A dance duet performed by two dancers, typically a male and a female.
 
• **Plié:** A fundamental ballet movement where the dancer bends their knees while keeping their back straight.
 
• **Arabesque:** A position in which the dancer stands on one leg with the other leg extended behind them.
 
 
 
• **New York City Ballet**
 
 
• Founded in 1948, it is one of the world's leading ballet companies.
 
• The company is known for performing Balanchine's works and showcasing innovative choreography.
 
 
 
• **Autobiographies by Dancers**
 
 
• Other notable autobiographies include *Life in Motion* by Misty Copeland and *Balancing Acts* by Patricia McBride.
 
• These books offer unique perspectives on the challenges and achievements in the world of dance.
